title: How RouterPlus uses AI agents to send contracts across its marketplace
summary: RouterPlus, a managed marketplace for AI inference, needed contracts with providers and customers from day zero. Its AI agents now send most of them through Common Paper, and it has onboarded more than 50 providers this fall.
body_markdown:
Since launching in fall 2026,[RouterPlus](https://routerplus.com/) has onboarded more than 50 inference providers and is enabling seven figures of deals. It’s one of the fastest growing companies on Common Paper. Each provider signs a Mutual NDA and a Data Processing Agreement, and the terms have to reflect where that provider processes data and which policies it follows. On the other side of the marketplace, RouterPlus needs contracts for customers starting a pilot or signing a longer-term deal.


Today, RouterPlus’s AI agents send most of those contracts through Common Paper. The team steps in when a deal calls for custom terms or human judgment.


## **Why RouterPlus moved beyond Word files and PDFs**


RouterPlus, a Y Combinator-backed marketplace for AI inference, needed contracts before it had its first customer. When it started on its first few deals, the team handle sending Word files and PDFs back and forth. But Alok Bishoyi, founder and CEO at RouterPlus, could see what was coming. Every new provider would need a familiar set of agreements, with a slightly customized terms.


The team first tried DocuSign but found it hard to manage and reuse templates. Bishoyi wanted a way to set up the agreements once and use them as new providers and customers came on board. He had his AI agent set up everything in Common Paper, then reviewed it himself.


## **What contracts go into a marketplace**


For a new provider, RouterPlus starts with the Common Paper[Mutual NDA](https://commonpaper.com/standards/mutual-nda/) . Bishoyi likes it because it’s easy for the other party to read and sign. The Data Processing Agreement is where the provider’s circumstances matter. Two providers can offer the same service and still need different language about how and where they handle data.


For a new customer, RouterPlus sends an NDA and a Data Processing Agreement, followed by a pilot agreement. If the pilot turns into a deal, the customer signs a Master Services Agreement (MSA). The commercial terms vary, too. One customer might pay per token while another reserves capacity or needs extra throughput for spikes in demand. RouterPlus uses a mix of standards and[its own custom contract templates](https://help.commonpaper.com/en/articles/16299870-using-your-own-contract-in-common-paper) .


## **How agents know when to send a contract**


RouterPlus’s internal agents use the context of a deal to recognize when an agreement is needed. That signal might be a customer expressing intent to move forward or an inference provider deciding to join the marketplace. Once the agent identifies the agreement and recipient, the contract goes out through Common Paper automatically through the[MCP](https://help.commonpaper.com/en/articles/14627004-common-paper-and-llms) .


> “95% of our contracts are handled entirely by agents.”
> Alok Bishoyi, RouterPlus


When needed, someone on the team handles a bespoke deal and makes sure any special terms are correctly represented in the final contract.


## **What changed for RouterPlus**


Bishoyi credits the setup with helping RouterPlus grow rapidly in its first few months. The team can reuse the templates he reviewed, account for differences between providers and send routine agreements through its agents. The same setup supports customer deals as they move from pilot to longer-term contracts.


> “We do seven figures of deals in inference contracts today, powered by Common Paper.”
> Alok Bishoyi, RouterPlus


As RouterPlus takes on larger customers, Bishoyi expects more negotiation and plans to hire sales and account management in the future. His advice for founders getting started is simple. Have your templates ready so that when both sides want to move forward, you can send the agreement and close right away.
